steps.what: Open the register for letters and parcels
Register, certify, and insure the accepted item
File the service against the item id

tasks.design: The service form for letters and parcels is opened from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk decides whether to register, certify, or insure the item, and says so. {DOCS} files that choice against the item id. The screen does not choose the service.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk copied the item id onto a paper service form.
tasks.enabler_now: The item id is already on the form.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the service, and refusing one the item does not qualify for, stays with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees the item and hears what the customer needs.

ambition.what: The form is open during the visit, and the clerk still chooses the service.

tasks.altitude: The clerk chooses before the service is filed.

evidence.claim: A form can be filed against an item id. Choosing register, certify, or insure stays with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a customer asks for a service and ends when the clerk has chosen and the choice is filed.
A service row has item id and the service code the clerk selected. An empty choice is not filed.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the item does not qualify for the service the customer asked for.
research_questions: Which items were registered, certified, or insured, and which were refused?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: The service the clerk chose for this item

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the item does not qualify and the clerk must refuse. High: the form is open and the clerk only chooses and files. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open forms for address changes and special services
Complete forms regarding theft, registered, or priority mail
Sign the completed form before filing

tasks.design: Forms for address changes, theft or loss, and special services such as registered or priority mail are opened from {DOCS}. The clerk completes the form from what the customer says. The clerk signs it before it is filed. A theft allegation is not created by the screen.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk fetched a blank and copied the same fields each time.
tasks.enabler_now: The blank is the stored form, so the fields are already named.
tasks.still_hard: Writing the customer's facts, and deciding whether a loss report is a theft report, stays with the clerk.

ambition.what: The right form is open during the visit, and the clerk still writes and signs the facts.

tasks.altitude: The clerk signs before the form is filed.

evidence.claim: A stored form can be opened with its fields named. The facts and the signature stay with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a customer needs a form and ends when the clerk has signed it or refused to file it.
A form template has form id and field names, owned by operations. The values are what the clerk typed. An empty required field blocks filing.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the customer's account does not fit the form.
research_questions: Which forms were signed, and which the clerk refused to file?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: The address, theft, or service facts the clerk wrote

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the account does not fit the form. High: the fields are known and the clerk writes and signs. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Receive letters and parcels at the counter
Place the received mail into bags
Show the bag label for this destination

tasks.design: The clerk receives letters and parcels and places them into bags. {OPS_SYSTEM} shows the bag label for the destination. The label does not move the mail.
tasks.enabler_now: The destination's bag label is stored.
tasks.still_hard: Receiving the item and placing it in the bag stay with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: The physical receive and bag work does not change.

evidence.claim: A stored bag label can be shown for a destination. Receiving and bagging stay with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when an item is handed over and ends when it is in the bag or refused.
A bag row has destination and label, set by the operations owner.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the destination has no bag.
research_questions: Which items were bagged, and which had no bag?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the destination has no bag. High: the label is shown and the clerk still receives and bags. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Retrieve parcels when customers claim them

tasks.design: Undelivered parcels are listed in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk puts them away and retrieves them when customers come to claim them. The clerk completes the related documentation and signs the handover. A parcel id that is not on the shelf is not marked claimed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The shelf list was a paper pad, and the clerk searched it.
tasks.enabler_now: The parcel id is on the list, so the shelf location is known.
tasks.still_hard: Putting the parcel away, recognising the customer, and handing it over stay with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees the person and the parcel.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still handles the parcel. The list only names the shelf.

reach.learn: Which parcel id was handed over.

evidence.claim: A stored parcel id can show a shelf location. The handover and the claim note stay with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a parcel cannot be delivered or a customer claims one and ends when it is shelved or handed over and the note is signed.
A parcel row has parcel id and shelf, written when the clerk shelved it. A claim note requires that id.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the person claiming is not the addressee.
research_questions: Which parcels were handed over, and which claims the clerk refused?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: The parcel id and the customer who claimed it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the claimant is not the addressee. High: the shelf is known and the clerk still retrieves and signs. The range stays under the net.
